newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BERLUSCONI SAYS SACCHI HAS MILAN'S BACKING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BERLUSCONI SAYS SACCHI HAS MILAN'S BACKING.

text.p: AC Milan owner Silvio Berlusconi has given coach Arrigo Sacchi his backing despite poor form that has left the Italian champions 12th in the league.
"He's not just a great coach but also a leader, an organiser, a modern man and we plan to continue with Sacchi," Sunday newspapers quoted Berlusconi as saying.
"It seems absurd to me to forecast the future. We have a contract with Sacchi and, I repeat, we want to respect it."

Sacchi, who presided over a golden period at the club in the 1980s, quit his job as Italian national team coach late last year and replaced Uruguayan Oscar Washington Tabarez who resigned as Milan's league and Cup form worsened.
Under Sacchi things have failed to improve and Milan were dumped out of the European Cup.

Italian newspapers have speculated at length in recent days that former Milan coach Fabio Capello, now coach of Spanish league leaders Real Madrid, was set to return to Italy at the end of the season for a variety of reasons.

Capello has said nothing about the rumours, which have variously linked him to Milan, local rivals Inter and Lazio. Inter and Lazio are both looking for new coaches for next season to replace Roy Hodgson and Zdenek Zeman respectively.
Berlusconi, asked how probable Capello's return was, replied: "Nothing is ruled out. There is only one thing that is certain: Capello will never go to Inter."
He said this was "because the collaboration between Capello and Milan and Berlusconi is not just based on a business relationship but on reciprocal friendship and loyalty."
Berlusconi also said that Milan were willing to help former Dutch star Marco van Basten should he need it.
"I spoke to him two or three months ago," said the billionaire media mogul and former prime minister.
"When he wants to dedicate himself to soccer we could offer various opportunities. But for the moment, Marco is just thinking about his physical recovery."
